meta.title: Timeline of World History
meta.year_convention: Historical years: negative = BCE, positive = CE, no year 0 (-1 = 1 BCE). end = null means ongoing at as_of.
meta.interval_convention: Half-open [start, end) at year resolution. A period runs from its start year up to, not including, its end year; adjacent periods share the boundary year.
meta.point_events: temporal_type 'point' marks something that happened within one year. year holds that year; start/end encode it as [year, year + 1) so it renders with width; end_label repeats the year.
meta.duration_rule: duration_years uses astronomical numbering (BCE year y -> y + 1) so spans across 1 BCE/1 CE are exact.
meta.uncertainty: start_approx and end_approx are independent flags.
meta.source_field: 'chart' = block shown on the poster; 'added' = added to complete it. chart_name keeps the poster's label where renamed; chart_value records known departures from the poster.
meta.verification_field: 'reviewed' = checked against the cited references; 'unsourced_standard_chronology' = standard historical chronology with no individual source.
meta.provenance_limit: Per-entry poster readings were not recorded during the original transcription, so chart_value appears only where a deliberate departure is known.
meta.applies_to: Every period, sub-period and affiliation lists the countries (by country_index name) it concerns, so shared tracks can be filtered by country.
meta.nesting: Nesting is a display grouping by time within one track, not political membership. relation says what a nested entry is: 'phase' (a stage of the parent), 'contemporary_polity' (a separate state existing at the same time), or 'interruption' (foreign rule or occupation breaking the parent). sub_periods are fully contained; related_periods overlap but extend beyond the parent.
meta.affiliations: Dated membership in a transregional empire, split around documented interruptions; each interval lies inside both the period and the empire; extent qualifies the tie (direct, partial, nominal, vassal...).
meta.empire_coverage: transregional_empires[].coverage is derived from the dated affiliations, per track and per country.

editorial_rules.tracks: scope = modern_territory when one state maps to the track; historical_region when several do. A track describes what happened in that territory, not one continuous state.
editorial_rules.top_level_periods: Top-level periods change with sovereignty (independence, unification, partition, annexation, colonial or foreign rule, satellite status) or state form (monarchy, republic, empire, new dynasty or shogunate). Regimes within one state form are sub-periods.
editorial_rules.poster_blocks: Poster blocks are kept intact even where they don't follow the rule above; changes inside them appear as sub-periods. Gaps between poster blocks are filled with top-level periods.
editorial_rules.occupations: Foreign occupations are top-level when they replaced the state, and parallel top-level periods when the state continued legally (e.g. a government in exile).
editorial_rules.indigenous_histories: Blocks before colonization are labelled 'Pre-colonial era' (poster: 'Indigenous Era'); Indigenous nations continue in parallel periods to the present.
editorial_rules.landmarks: Each landmark has its own date and is attached to the period containing that date; poster_period_id keeps the poster's placement where it differs.
editorial_rules.achievement_attribution: tracks = modern territory where the work was done or, for voyages and programmes, where it was organized. Contributors' nationality is noted separately when it differs.
editorial_rules.transregional_empires: A reusable registry of polities that appear in two or more tracks, plus major colonial empires.

completeness_review.statement: All continents are represented. The country index maps all 193 UN member states, the 2 UN observers and the main disputed territories to tracks; each entry states which periods apply to it and whether coverage has gaps. Historical detail varies by country.
completeness_review.poster_scope: 21 modern countries, c. 3000 BCE to 2000 CE, 30 milestones. The poster calls itself a simplified view.
limits: Regional tracks summarize several countries; national detail varies.
Most dates follow standard chronology without individual sources; see provenance.

changes: Point events: 11 single-year records now use temporal_type 'point' instead of empty [Y, Y) intervals.
Magna Graecia promoted to a top-level parallel period; related periods now always overlap their parent.
Country applicability: applies_to on every period, sub-period and affiliation; country_index lists the periods for each country, coverage level and gaps.
Added real histories for Andorra, Monaco, Liechtenstein, San Marino, the Holy See, Lesotho, Eswatini, South Sudan, Kosovo, Eritrea, Panama, Belize, Yemen, Oman and the Gulf states.
Tracks holding several states renamed and rescoped as historical regions (e.g. 'Romania and Moldova', 'Sudan and South Sudan').

Affiliations split around documented interruptions (Persian and Byzantine Egypt, Ottoman Egypt, Iraq, Serbia and Cuba, Soviet Ukraine) and marked nominal where rule was nominal (Abbasid Iran and Egypt, late Mughal India and Pakistan).
Nested entries carry a relation (phase, contemporary_polity, interruption); nesting is defined as display grouping, not membership.

Corrections: Yangshao and Longshan separated; Liangzhu c. 3300–2300 BCE; Piast royal line ends 1370 with Angevin Poland added; Central American independence, Mexican Empire and federation separated with correct member states; Antarctic Treaty System from 1961; COVID-19 entry renamed to the WHO emergency.
Semantics: Cueva de las Manos, L'Anse aux Meadows and the Royal court in Brazil reclassified; UK 1917 block renamed 'House of Windsor'; 'European arrival in the Americas (Columbus)' label.
Verification status renamed to 'unsourced_standard_chronology'; status added to events, landmarks and empires; provenance counts published.
Full continental coverage (57 new tracks), country_index and continent field, 7 registry empires, 6 events.
Date fixes after the first review; schema rebuild (contained sub-periods, dated affiliations, landmark registry, entity types, uncertainty, durations); 23 tracks, events layer, achievements.
Transcribed the poster; added 20 tracks, 3 empires, 13 milestones.

changelog.change: Americas: pre-colonial blocks split into the civilisations and cultures they contained (Olmec, Teotihuacan, Toltec, Aztec, Maya, Mississippian, Puebloans, Chinchorro, Taíno and others).
Wikipedia article added to every event and achievement.

Early Americas and Africa: long blocks split into documented phases (Archaic, Formative, Olmec, Preclassic Maya, Valdivia to La Tolita, Green and Pastoral Sahara, Tichitt, Kintampo, Bantu homeland and expansion, Khoisan foragers) and empty early centuries filled (Sahel millet farmers, forest foragers, Pastoral Neolithic herders, Ethiopian highland farmers, Amazigh ancestors, San foragers).
